landing.ctaTitle: Someone in your family still remembers.
landing.ctaBody: Start the living story today — adding the first person takes a minute, and the rest of the family can join you.
landing.pricingTitle: Simple pricing, for the whole family.
landing.archiveFeatures: Unlimited family members|Unlimited photos & stories|Full timeline|Collaboration & roles|Private family space|Search
landing.privacyTitle: Your family's story stays your family's.
landing.privateBody: Every family archive is its own closed space. Nothing is public unless you publish it.
landing.rolesBody: Owners, editors, contributors and viewers — each gets exactly the access they need.
landing.inviteBody: Family joins by a personal invitation or a private link, never an open sign-up.
landing.startSubcopy: You don't need the whole tree on day one. Grandparents remember the beginning, parents fill in the middle — you only have to start.
landing.step1Body: Your name and year of birth. That's the whole first step.
landing.step2Body: The tree starts to take shape the moment there's a second generation.
landing.step3Body: A photo, a date, a sentence someone once told you.
landing.step4Body: They fill in what you don't know — the tree grows from both ends.
landing.metaTitle: Root house — Create the living story of your family
landing.metaDescription: A private home for your family's people, photos and stories. Build the tree, keep the memories behind it, and invite the relatives who remember.
landing.heroLead: The people, photos and stories that make your family yours — kept together in one private place, and passed on.

fragments.paul: Dear Paul, the lake froze early this year…

landing.memoryProblem: The photos are there. Who's in them — only grandma remembers.
landing.memoryAnswer: Root house gives every memory a person to belong to.
landing.showcaseTitle: A person is more than a name and two dates.

tree.title: A family tree that grows with you
tree.body: Add people one at a time and the tree lays itself out — couples side by side, children under their parents, every branch where you'd expect it.

profile.title: A page for every person
profile.body: Where they were born and lived, what they did, the photos they're in and the stories people tell about them — all on one page.

photos.title: Photos that know who's in them
photos.body: Tag the people in an old photo and it appears on each of their pages. Hover a face to see who it is.

lifeline.title: A life on one line
lifeline.body: Births, moves, weddings and everything in between, laid out on a single line from the first year to the last.

stories.title: Stories from the ones who remember
stories.body: Write down what grandma told you about the winter of 1947 and link it to everyone who was there.

kinship.title: How exactly are we related?
kinship.body: Pick any two people and see the path between them — and what to call each other.

panel.uncle: Paul is your uncle — your mother's brother
panel.moveStory: Ivan found work at the port; Vera followed with the children's things in two suitcases.
panel.storyBody: Mum always said the lake froze so hard that winter that the whole village walked across it to church. She was sixteen, and it was the first time she saw my father — on the ice, carrying someone else's skates.
